text:
elaine: heads-up — multiple customers hitting timeouts and 5xxs on the ranking endpoint for ~20m, p95 shot to ~3.2s, a few 502/504s reported. request-id examples: r1234, r1235. :rotating_light:

mike: seen it too. p95 spike correlates with a traffic burst to /v1/ranking at 10:14 UTC. frontline logs show nginx upstream timed out and haproxy queue_burst. :eyes:

ash: I'm seeing a lot of gateway retries from the gateway to ranker-service, we might be thrashing the pool. snippet from gateway logs:

```
2026-03-17T10:14:35Z gateway ERROR route=/v1/ranking upstream_status=504 upstream_response_time=1200ms retries=2 queue_time=450ms req_id=r1234
2026-03-17T10:14:36Z gateway WARN route=/v1/ranking upstream_status=502 backend_error="killed-worker" req_id=r1235
```

jordan: customer repro steps they sent (sanitized):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ranking \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"best wireless earbuds","candidates":[...180 items...],"top_k":10}'
```

frank: important — their payload included ~180 candidates, each with long metadata fields. our reranker max_candidates default is 200 but internal batching + scoring cost is high for large candidate lists. suspect CPU/GPU contention + KV cache thrash.

elaine: good call. can we confirm if quantized ranker variant (ranker-v2-quant-q4) was rolled out to that cluster? quant variant has different perf under long sequences.

mike: checked model routing table — traffic split 80/20 v2/v2-quant on cluster us-west-2-prod-g1. at burst time the quant nodes had higher backlog and OOM-kill on the scoring worker, causing 502s.

ash: immediate mitigations proposed:
- set gateway retry to linear backoff and reduce max retries to 1 for /v1/ranking
- temporarily pin affected customers to ranker-v2 (non-quant) via routing rules
- throttle candidate count at edge: enforce 100 candidate limit and return 400 with guidance
- raise worker pool for ranker service by +2 replicas in cluster

mike: doing the routing pin now (canary to 5 customers). also raising pod replicas for ranker-service in us-west-2 to handle backlog.

frank: we should add a quick server-side validation rejecting >120 candidates with a clear error and docs link. that will stop accidental large payloads.

elaine: support-bot: escalate to billing? one customer reported spike in cost due to retries.

support-bot: flagged to billing, ticket #B-5543 created.

jordan: follow-ups for postmortem:
- capture full request size distribution for /v1/ranking over last 24h
- add alert when queue_time > 300ms for 3m and gateway 5xx rate > 0.5%
- investigate why quant variant fails under long candidate lists (memory leak or kernel regressions)
- add automatic fallback to non-quant model on backend OOM/worker-kill

ash: repro note: I reproduced locally by sending 150 candidates with long metadata strings and got 502 within 30s. command I used:

```
python tools/loadtest.py --endpoint /v1/ranking --concurrency 20 --payload tests/payloads/long_candidates_150.json
```

mike: after pin and replica bump, 5xxs dropped to normal within ~2min. p95 back to ~420ms. customers reported success. :thumbsup:

elaine: will file follow-up tickets:
- INF-1298: add candidate_count validation + user-facing error (assigned ash)
- INF-1299: quant variant memory regression investigation (assigned jordan)
- INF-1300: gateway retry/backoff tuning (assigned mike)

frank: quick note for support replies: include this snippet to suggest workaround to users until fix is out:
```
- reduce candidate list to <= 100
- or set "top_k" appropriately to avoid huge candidate lists
- contact support to get customer routed to non-quant ranker temporarily
```

elaine: thanks team. adding postmortem label and scheduling 1hr follow-up sync. :calendar:
